Subject: CAIQ evidence transport — initial ask and tagging requirements

Hi David,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing the CAIQ submission package for our internal cloud assurance team and need to ingest several runtime artifacts from Redwood for a subset of controls (primarily telemetry, key management, and tenant isolation proofs). Before we schedule a pickup, we wanted to confirm two things so our intake system can process files without manual rework:

1) Preferred transport mechanism — SFTP vs secure Share (Drive link) vs encrypted S3 presigned objects.
2) Tenant tagging/metadata schema — we need a short JSON schema or CSV header that indicates tenant_id, model_variant, region, retention_window_days, and assertion_reference.

A couple of constraints from our side: our auditor (cc'd) needs immutable names on files (no renaming during upload), and we will require SHA256 checksums for any log bundles.

Can you confirm the recommended approach and whether Redwood can seed the attachments with the tenant metadata as a header row? If helpful, we're available for a short — 30 minute — sync this week.

Thanks —
Asha Verma
Security Ops Manager
AcmeOps

Asha — thanks for the clear ask. Short answers up front: we can support all three transport options you listed; our recommended default is encrypted S3 presigned objects (time-limited, programmatic checksums) with a mirrored secure Drive share if you need a UI for review. We will include an initial metadata header on each artifact.

Proposed minimal protocol (we'll provide a one-page spec PDF):
- Upload method: primary = encrypted S3 presigned upload (AES-256 at rest). Fallback = Drive link (restricted share).
- File naming: <acct>-<tenant_id>-<control>-<YYYYMMDD>-<sequence>.tgz (we'll seed names, you must accept unchanged).
- Metadata header: CSV/JSON top-level with fields: tenant_id, model_variant, region, retention_window_days, assertion_reference, evidence_owner (email), capture_time_iso. We recommend JSON-lines for log bundles.
- Checksums: SHA256 provided in <filename>.sha256 alongside bundle.
- Retention note: for CAIQ we recommend retention_window_days >= 90 for runtime traces; we can mark shorter where necessary.

Action items for Redwood: we'll produce a templated "transport_instructions.pdf" and a seed index file (acmeops_caiq_evidence_index.xlsx) that includes the header columns and example rows.

Can Kimberly and Marissa weigh in on the metadata schema specifics (especially when we need redaction or sampled logs vs full traces)? If that looks good, I can create the Drive folder and pre-generate a set of presigned URLs for your test upload.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

--

Thanks David — a few practical clarifications from engineering/security side: 

- Tenant tagging: we can add a top-level JSON manifest per bundle named <bundle>.manifest.json. That manifest will contain the fields you requested plus an array field "files" with filename, sha256, and a minimal mime-type. That avoids having to change binary names post-upload.
- Sampling vs full traces: for PII/PI-sensitive environments we'll produce sampled traces and include a sampling_rate field in the manifest. If AcmeOps requires full traces for a particular control, we need an explicit approval (email thread) to widen access.
- Key evidence: KMS rotation logs and HSM attestation are exported as PDFs and will be zipped with the manifest; we will not include private key material.
- Checksum automation: presigned S3 + multipart upload implies checksums for each part; we will provide a consolidated SHA256 computed after assemble.

One ask for the auditor: what format do you prefer for assertion_reference? We use internal claim IDs (e.g., CAIQ-RED-2025-####). If you need your own Crosswalk ID, we can map both in the manifest.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
